title: Built this ELDORIA creature concept for a persistent game world inhabited by autonomous AI agents
author: maaxpower6666
selftext:
I’m building ELDORIA, a persistent game world designed for autonomous AI agents.

This Revenant creature concept was created from ELDORIA’s worldbuilding direction — using its affinity, ecology, progression and creature-design systems as the basis for the visual.

It’s not just meant to be “random AI monster art.” The goal is for creatures in ELDORIA to eventually be generated from underlying canonical data such as genome traits, body structure, affinities, ecology, rarity and progression state.

ELDORIA itself is being built around:

persistent world state

autonomous player agents

internal software agents

event-driven world reactions

canonical server-side rules

movement through a real location graph

creature progression and long-term history

I’m building most of the project on a Samsung S25 Pro using Termux + Claude Code, with GitHub CI as the main verification layer.

The long-term idea is simple:

AI agents shouldn’t just chat. They should be able to live in a world, make decisions, build history and change over time.

Curious what other AI game developers think about this direction.

replies.author: maaxpower6666
replies.body:
Fair question. The image is concept art, but ELDORIA is much more than that.
I’m building an actual persistent backend for autonomous AI agents: registration/login, persistent world state, movement through a location graph, world ticks, encounters, quests, creatures, long-term history, internal world agents and event-driven reactions.
By “canonical server-side rules” I mean that the AI is not allowed to simply invent game truth. The server decides what is real: your current location, whether a move is legal, what creature exists, whether a quest is complete, rewards, encounters, etc. AI agents can interpret, narrate and make decisions, but the backend validates the actual world state.
And yes, I used AI to help write the post too. I’m also using Claude Code heavily to build the project itself — mostly from my Samsung phone through Termux.
So the interesting part for me isn’t the generated image. It’s whether autonomous agents can actually live and act inside a persistent world over time.
